---
title: "Regression: complete modelling workflow"
---

```{r}
# Load packages
library(readr)
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(broom)


# Load data
insurance <- read_csv("data/insuranceKaggle.csv")


# 1. Inspect the data -----------------------------------------------------

glimpse(insurance)

summary(insurance %>% select(age, charges))


# 2. Explore the response variable ---------------------------------------

ggplot(insurance, aes(x = charges)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Insurance Charges",
    x = "Charges",
    y = "Number of observations"
  )


# 3. Visualize the relationship between age and charges ------------------

ggplot(insurance, aes(x = age, y = charges)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Insurance Charges versus Age",
    x = "Age",
    y = "Insurance charges"
  )


# 4. Split the data into training and testing sets -----------------------

set.seed(123)

insurance_split <- initial_split(
  insurance,
  prop = 0.80
)

insurance_train <- training(insurance_split)
insurance_test  <- testing(insurance_split)


# 5. Specify the linear regression model ---------------------------------

lm_spec <- linear_reg() %>%
  set_engine("lm")


# 6. Fit the model using the training data -------------------------------

lm_fit <- lm_spec %>%
  fit(
    charges ~ age,
    data = insurance_train
  )


# 7. Examine the fitted model --------------------------------------------

tidy(lm_fit)


# 8. Generate predictions for the test data -------------------------------

results <- insurance_test %>%
  bind_cols(
    predict(lm_fit, new_data = insurance_test)
  )


# 9. Examine observed and predicted charges ------------------------------

results %>%
  select(age, charges, .pred) %>%
  head(10)


# 10. Evaluate predictive performance ------------------------------------

metrics(
  results,
  truth = charges,
  estimate = .pred
)

rmse(results, truth = charges, estimate = .pred)

mae(results, truth = charges, estimate = .pred)

rsq(results, truth = charges, estimate = .pred)


# 11. Plot observed versus predicted charges ------------------------------

ggplot(results, aes(x = charges, y = .pred)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(
    intercept = 0,
    slope = 1,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Observed versus Predicted Insurance Charges",
    x = "Observed charges",
    y = "Predicted charges"
  )


# 12. Examine residuals --------------------------------------------------

diagnostics <- augment(lm_fit$fit)

ggplot(diagnostics, aes(x = .fitted, y = .resid)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Residuals versus Fitted Values",
    x = "Fitted charges",
    y = "Residuals"
  )


# 13. Normal Q-Q plot ----------------------------------------------------

ggplot(diagnostics, aes(sample = .std.resid)) +
  stat_qq() +
  stat_qq_line() +
  labs(
    title = "Normal Q-Q Plot of Standardized Residuals"
  )
```




# Regression: Complete Modelling Workflow

```{r}
# Load packages
library(readr)
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(broom)


# Load data
insurance <- read_csv("data/insuranceKaggle.csv")


# 1. Inspect the data -----------------------------------------------------

glimpse(insurance)

summary(insurance %>% select(age, charges))


# 2. Explore the response variable ---------------------------------------

ggplot(insurance, aes(x = charges)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Insurance Charges",
    x = "Charges",
    y = "Number of observations"
  )


# 3. Visualize the relationship between age and charges ------------------

ggplot(insurance, aes(x = age, y = charges)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Insurance Charges versus Age",
    x = "Age",
    y = "Insurance charges"
  )


# 4. Split the data into training and test sets ---------------------------

set.seed(123)

insurance_split <- initial_split(
  insurance,
  prop = 0.80
)

insurance_train <- training(insurance_split)
insurance_test  <- testing(insurance_split)


# 5. Specify the linear regression model ----------------------------------

lm_spec <- linear_reg() %>%
  set_engine("lm")


# 6. Fit the model using the training data -------------------------------

lm_fit <- lm_spec %>%
  fit(
    charges ~ age,
    data = insurance_train
  )


# 7. Examine the fitted model ---------------------------------------------

tidy(lm_fit)


# 8. Generate predictions for the training data ---------------------------

train_results <- insurance_train %>%
  bind_cols(
    predict(lm_fit, new_data = insurance_train)
  )


# 9. Generate predictions for the test data -------------------------------

test_results <- insurance_test %>%
  bind_cols(
    predict(lm_fit, new_data = insurance_test)
  )


# 10. Compare training and test performance -------------------------------

regression_metrics <- metric_set(
  rmse,
  mae,
  rsq,
  mape
)

regression_metrics(
  train_results,
  truth = charges,
  estimate = .pred
)

regression_metrics(
  test_results,
  truth = charges,
  estimate = .pred
)


# 11. Examine observed and predicted charges ------------------------------

test_results %>%
  select(age, charges, .pred) %>%
  head(10)


# 12. Plot observed versus predicted charges ------------------------------

ggplot(test_results, aes(x = charges, y = .pred)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(
    intercept = 0,
    slope = 1,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Observed versus Predicted Insurance Charges",
    x = "Observed charges",
    y = "Predicted charges"
  )


# 13. Examine residuals on the training data ------------------------------

diagnostics <- augment(lm_fit$fit)

ggplot(diagnostics, aes(x = .fitted, y = .resid)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Residuals versus Fitted Values",
    x = "Fitted charges",
    y = "Residuals"
  )


# 14. Normal Q-Q plot -----------------------------------------------------

ggplot(diagnostics, aes(sample = .std.resid)) +
  stat_qq() +
  stat_qq_line() +
  labs(
    title = "Normal Q-Q Plot of Standardized Residuals"
  )
```
